newsitem.title: USA: U.S. High Court rejects White House appeal on notes.
newsitem.headline: U.S. High Court rejects White House appeal on notes.

text.p: The U.S. Supreme Court on Monday rejected a White House appeal arguing that notes by its lawyers on talks with first lady Hillary Rodham Clinton should be kept from Whitewater prosecutors.

The justices let stand a U.S. appeals court ruling that the attorney-client privilege does not apply to the notes, which had been subpoenaed by Whitewater independent counsel Kenneth Starr as part of his grand jury investigation.
The Supreme Court's action, taken without any explanation or dissent, means the notes will have to be surrendered.
The action was a major defeat for the White House, for Mrs. Clinton and for the Clinton Justice Department, all of which urged the high court to hear the case.

Starr has conducted a long investigation into Whitewater, a complex web of Arkansas business deals involving the Clintons, and allegations of a later coverup. President Bill Clinton and his wife have not been accused of any wrongdoing.

At issue are conversations Mrs. Clinton had on July 11, 1995, and on January 26, 1996, concerning her role in Whitewater. White House lawyers took the notes while Mrs. Clinton talked with her private Whitewater attorney, David Kendall.
